task: MySQL dialect: MySQL allows setting the auto-increment counter of an existing table with `ALTER TABLE t AUTO_INCREMENT=3000000000`. sqlglot already parses `AUTO_INCREMENT` as a table property in `CREATE TABLE`. Support it in `ALTER TABLE` too, parsed as the same auto-increment property and round-tripping.
why:
The source changes are identical, so test fidelity to the request decided it. The task asks for two things: the statement must be "parsed as the same auto-increment property" and must round-trip. c1 tests both. It adds an identity round-trip test and an AST check that the ALTER action is an `exp.AutoIncrementProperty` with the value `3000000000`.
The runner-up, c2, only adds the identity round-trip. A round-trip test would still pass if the statement were wrongly parsed into a generic or command node, so the "same property" requirement goes unchecked.
